<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Setting up Gradle 9.7.1 and JDK 21 for the backend build.

Spring Boot 3.5.16 is selected to match the 3.x requirement and work with Gradle 9.7.1. The backend will be scaffolded in a `backend/` directory using Kotlin DSL Gradle files and the Gradle wrapper.

The Gradle wrapper will be generated after the initial files are created. The build script will include Spring Web, Validation, Data JPA, Flyway, PostgreSQL, H2, Actuator, and SpringDoc. Tests will use JUnit, Testcontainers, and MockMvc. SQL migrations will be compatible with both H2 and PostgreSQL. A TicketStatus domain enum with ALLOWED values is planned.

Domain design now includes TicketPriority, Ticket, Comment, and TicketStatusHistory entities with transition logic. Repositories will use Spring Data Specifications for search. Services will cover ticket, comment, and state transitions. DTOs will be records. Controllers will use a global exception handler returning ProblemDetail. CORS configuration is planned. Parameterized tests and integration tests are also included. The next step is to create the backend directory and generate the Gradle wrapper.

Flyway migrations will use portable SQL compatible with both H2 and PostgreSQL. The exact schema will be verified against the data model. The package layout is now defined across common, ticket, and comment modules. The project will be built incrementally and validated with ./gradlew build.

An ErrorCodes enum will standardize error responses. Docker Compose and environment examples were considered but skipped to keep the scope backend-only. Transition notes will be validated as required when a ticket moves to RESOLVED or CANCELLED. Creating a ticket will automatically log a history row from null to OPEN. Comment counts will be fetched via @Formula or repository subqueries. List endpoints will return a compact TicketSummaryResponse without descriptions. A custom PageResponse record will wrap paginated results. Files will be written in batches starting with the backend directory and Gradle wrapper.
</details></think>
